"I used to find the owl endurable," said she, "but since the war I have found him unbearable. He hoots all night and makes me so depressed that I feel that I shall go mad."

"And so you come and listen to the owl in London?" I said.

"Yes," I said, "the owl that hoots in Carmelite Street and Printing House Square."

message.content:
A rather gloomy individual. Numerous people find him an unbearable presence. I had a conversation during dinner in London a few evenings ago with a woman who owns a home in Sussex, and I discovered she hadn’t visited there in quite a while.

"I used to find the owl somewhat tolerable," she remarked, "but ever since the war, I’ve found him utterly intolerable. He hoots all night and plunges me into such despair that I feel I might lose my mind."

"So, you choose to listen to the owl while in London?" I inquired.

"The owl in London?" she responded, puzzled.

"Yes," I clarified, "the owl that hoots near Carmelite Street and Printing House Square."

"Ah," she replied, "but that owl is such a ridiculous one. The owl in the countryside, however, is far more grave."

"He expresses a rather foolish idea with such gravity," I interjected.

"Indeed, but in the stillness and darkness, it feels as if there’s no response to him."

"My dear lady," I suggested, "if you cast your gaze upwards at the stars, you might discover a rather thorough answer."

I must admit, I find the owl not just bearable but invigorating. I appreciate hearing the pessimist fully express his views. It is the vague, undefined anxieties of the mind that can paralyze us, yet when my owl voices the bleakest outlook, I start to feel uplifted, ready to confront challenges. Is this the worst that can be articulated? Then let us explore the best possibilities and strive to achieve them. "The task is impossible," declared the pessimist to Cobden. "Indeed," Cobden replied. "Then the sooner we embark on it, the better." Oh, I say to my owl, everything is lost, is it? Just wait until dawn, and listen to what that little fellow in the red waistcoat has to say. He has a much more hopeful narrative to share, one that is far more plausible than yours. I’ll retreat to bed now and leave you to Gummidge in the trees until sunlight arrives and reveals what a dismal fraud you truly are.
